messages:
Ben (Support): Hey team — customer reported sudden 401 invalid_api_key starting ~09:12 UTC after they rotated keys. They say nothing changed in their app other than rotating the secret in their k8s cluster. stack: Node.js api using REDWOOD_API_KEY env var. sample curl they sent: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate`

Maya (Support): Can you paste the first 8 chars of the key they rotated to (we only need a fingerprint), and confirm whether they used our \"Authorization: Bearer\" header or the x-api-key header?

Ben (Support): They sent: `starts with: red_9f2b7a1c`. They say they used Authorization: Bearer. Also shared a pod env dump (redacted):
```
REACT_APP_REDWOOD_KEY=\"red_9f2b7a1c...\"
```

Carmen Li (Eng): Two quick suspects: 1) quotes/newline accidentally embedded in the secret (common when using `kubectl create secret generic --from-file` on Windows or if the value was double-quoted in YAML), 2) app still reading the old secret due to k8s secret version reference or missing rollout. Ask them to exec into the pod and `echo -n $REACT_APP_REDWOOD_KEY | hexdump -C | sed -n '1,2p'` to check for trailing CR/LF or quotes.

Ben (Support): Asked customer to run that, they replied with this output:
```
00000000  72 65 64 5f 39 66 32 62  37 61 31 63 3a 2e 2e 2e  |red_9f2b7a1c:...|
00000010  5c 6e                                             |\\n|
```

Kira (DevEx): That `5c 6e` means a literal backslash + n sequence in the secret (i.e. the string contains `\\n`), not an actual newline. Looks like the secret value was inserted with an escaped newline (maybe they pasted the literal `\\n` when exporting from a Windows tool or included quotes). If the application sends `Authorization: Bearer red_9f2b7a1c\\n` the server will reject it (token mismatch).

Maya (Support): Also, note our token validation trims whitespace but does not strip literal `\\n` sequences. Can you ask them to confirm the exact YAML used to create the secret? common bad patterns: `value: "red_...\n"` or using `echo "${KEY}" > file` which can include `\\n`.

Ben (Support): Customer pasted their k8s secret yaml (sanitized):
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: redwood-creds
type: Opaque
data:
  REDWOOD_API_KEY: cmVkXzlmMmI3YTFlOj09XG5=  # base64 encoded of `red_9f2b7a1c::=\\n`
```

Carmen Li (Eng): Base64 shows `5c 6e` earlier which matches `\\n`. Fix: update the secret to remove the escaped newline and restart pods. Quick repro steps we can give them:
1) Decode locally to confirm: `echo cmVkXzlmMmI3YTFlOj09XG4= | base64 -d --wrap=0 | sed -n '1,2p'` (they should see `red_9f2b7a1c::=` with no `\\n`)
2) If they used a CI step like `printf "%s" \"$KEY\"` instead of `echo`, that avoids adding `\\n`.

Ben (Support): I shared both suggestions. Customer tried replacing the secret with a cleaned value (they used `printf '%s' "$KEY" | base64`) and restarted the deployment. Their follow-up: "looks like it worked, no more 401s" :tada:. They also said their CI pipeline had been exporting the key with an extra literal `\\n` when writing to the secret file prior to base64.

Kira (DevEx): Good catch. I'll add a short note to the k8s quickstart doc about ensuring secrets are created without escaped/newline characters and a snippet recommending `printf '%s' "$KEY" | base64 -w0` for Linux and `printf '%s' "$KEY" | base64` for mac.

Carmen Li (Eng): For future protection we could relax token parsing to strip common escaped sequences when validating (e.g., convert `\\n` -> ''), but that might hide app bugs. Filing a small RFC?

deploy-bot: Deployment redeploy-redwood-api triggered by Ben (Support) — status: success

Maya (Support): Closing this thread — root cause: literal escaped newline (`\\n`) in k8s secret due to CI export, manifested as malformed token. Workaround: recreate secret without escaped characters and restart. Follow-ups: Kira to update docs, Carmen to consider validation RFC.

Ben (Support): Added a note to the customer's ticket with the steps and the fix. Thanks everyone.
